topic.title: Data Field Encapsulation
topic.description: Hiding data with getters and setters

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how to keep your code's data safe from accidental changes? Let's explore data field encapsulation!

• Why hiding data is a good thing
• How getters and setters work like bouncers
• How to protect your class's private parts (data!)

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine your class is a VIP nightclub. The data fields are the VIP guests inside. You wouldn't let just anyone walk in and mess with them, right?

That's where encapsulation comes in - it's like having bouncers (getters/setters) who control who gets access to what.

• **Private fields**: The VIP guests (data) that stay hidden
• **Public methods**: The bouncers (getters/setters) who control access
• **Validation**: The guest list that checks who's allowed in

sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Data Field Encapsulation works:

steps.title: The Problem
steps.description: Without encapsulation, anyone can mess with your data directly. This is like letting strangers into the VIP section!

steps.title: Adding Protection
steps.description: Make the field private and add controlled access points. Now only approved changes get through!

steps.title: Using It Safely
steps.description: Now the data is protected, and we can add rules like validation. The VIP guests are safe!
steps.code:
Person p = new Person();
p.setName("Alice"); // Works
p.setName(""); // Ignored - validation!
System.out.println(p.getName()); // Safe access

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Private fields hide data from outside access
✓ Getters let you read data safely
✓ Setters let you modify data with control
✓ Encapsulation = data + methods that work on it

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Add getters for all fields you need to read
Add setters only when you need to modify
donts: Don't forget to validate in setters
sections.protip: Use your IDE's 'Generate Getters/Setters' feature to save time, but always review the generated code!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Data Field Encapsulation used in real apps?

examples.how: Account balances are private - you can't just change them! Only specific methods (like deposit/withdraw) can modify them with proper validation.
User data like passwords are private. Setters validate new passwords meet security requirements before changing them.
Player health is private - you can't just set it to 1000! Only specific game events (like healing potions) can modify it.

problem.description: Create a `BankAccount` class with encapsulation. It should have a private `balance` field that can't be accessed directly. Add methods to deposit, withdraw, and check balance. Withdrawals should fail if there's not enough money.
hints: Add validation in withdraw to check balance
getBalance should just return the current balance
problem.explanation: The balance is protected from direct access. Deposits only work with positive amounts. Withdrawals check for sufficient funds. The balance can only be read, not modified directly.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Encapsulation hides data and exposes controlled access points
📌 Always make fields private and add getters/setters as needed
📌 Use setters to validate data before changing it
📌 Practice by encapsulating real-world objects like bank accounts!
